To: Supply Chain and Sustainability Leadership
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing cost and carbon in warehouse-to-store shipments
Date: Current planning cycle

Context
We are preparing the next distribution plan across our warehouse-to-store network. Each shipping lane is measured on two outcomes: the variable monetary cost per unit and the carbon emissions per unit. The reality is that the lowest-cost lanes often carry higher carbon intensity, while cleaner options can be more expensive. We need a defensible approach that balances short-term cost discipline with our commitments to decarbonization and brand reputation.

Operational rules
- Route activation costs: Opening a lane requires a one-time setup expense tied to contracting, compliance, and dock readiness. A lane is either active or not; once active, the setup cost applies regardless of how much we ship.
- Minimum order quantities: If we activate a lane, we must move at least a defined load size on it. Partial loads are not accepted, so small opportunistic shipments are not feasible on that lane.
- Supplier limits per store: To protect receiving capacity and keep vendor management practical, each store may be supplied by only a limited number of warehouses. This cap means we must consolidate volumes and be selective about which lanes we open per store.

Network requirements
- Warehouse supply: Shipments from each warehouse cannot exceed available inventory.
- Store demand: Each store’s minimum demand must be met in full and on time.
- Feasibility: Any activated lane must carry at least its minimum order, and each store must receive from no more than the allowed number of warehouses.

Management priority
Leadership has set the relative importance of cost versus emissions. Our evaluation will blend the total variable shipping cost and total emissions using these importance weights. Route setup costs will be added in full to this blended score; they are not scaled by the importance weights. This approach makes the cost–carbon trade-off explicit while ensuring we do not over-activate lanes that add overhead without sufficient benefit.

Goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each active lane to deliver the lowest blended total under real operating conditions. The plan must:
- Respect warehouse supply limits and satisfy all store demand requirements.
- Use active lanes efficiently by meeting or exceeding their minimum order quantities.
- Keep the number of supplying warehouses per store within the allowed cap.
- Balance variable cost and emissions according to management’s weights while accounting for all one-time setup costs.

This framework will produce a practical, execution-ready shipping plan that aligns with both our financial targets and our sustainability commitments. It will also highlight where small changes in weights, minimum orders, or supplier caps materially change the recommended lanes, enabling transparent trade-off discussions with Finance, Sustainability, and Operations.
